newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares finished weaker but off day's lows, trickling down on Wall Street's overnight slide after its recent bullish run, dealers said.
They said some profit-taking on some shares had also taken place through most of the day ahead of the weekend, stunting gains.
Dealers added that although Wall Street had weighed down the market's upward pace, the Dow had been largely ignored in late dealings when it opened around 100 points down at the close of local trade.
"There has been some nice trade going through. The market has generally been down on the day, on the back of the Dow, but I don't think the Dow is really going to do too much," one dealer said.
The industrial index ended down 5.0 points at 9,145.5, as the all-share index closed off 27.7 points at 7,456.8.
Golds also ended off on the back of an ailing bullion price, which was last bid at $323.90 an ounce.
The gold index lost 18.1 points to 963.7 points.

Among gold mining firms which took a knock from bullion's woes were Western Areas, Kloof and Vaal Reefs, which ended off 90 cents at 29.50 rand, 60 cents at 23.40 rand and 375 cents at 235.00 rand, respectively.
"I think it's also been a usual Friday with no real direction," one dealer at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said.
"I will say there has been a little bit of good underlying buying coming in on weakness," the dealer added.
In the broader market decliners led advancers by 237 to 157, while 16 shares dropped to new lows and 26 surged to new highs.
Mining firm Maranda closed up 20 cents at 480 cents on news it was part of a consortium which had been awarded a Zambian copper project.
Maranda's stock earlier peaked to a new 12-month high of 490 cents while newly-listed base metals firm Billiton ended 10 cents down on big volumes amid continued listing interest, dealers said.

Day's turnover in Billiton were at 25.7 million rand after its underwriters said they exercised the manager's option to subscribe for a further 56.20 million ordinary shares at the placing price of 220 pence.
Following the exercise of the option, the total size of the international placing offer was 431.25 million ordinary shares amounting to 949 million stg, the firm said in a published notice.

Continued buying interest from offshore was evident in industrial firm Barlows which saw an offshore buyer taking 570,000 shares in an overnight deal valued at around 34 million rand by brokers Merrill Lynch.
Barlows, however, ended down 100 cents at 58.50 rand with volumes at 48.3 million rand.

Supermarket firm Pick 'n Pay was unchanged at 816 cent after stockbrokers ING Barings sold 500,000 shares for four million rand to brokers Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, and 817,000 shares worth six million rand to brokers UBS Securities.
Dealers said underlying sentiment on the market remained positive and expected next week's direction to continue upward with all eyes fixed on clues for interest rate cut prospects.
On the futures side, Wall Street's shaky start sent near-dated industrial contracts off with no help coming from a weaker bond market and a troubled rand.
The September industrial contract was last at 8,640/46 from 8,699, the gold contract was at 682/90 from 702 and the all-share contract was at 6,692/705 from 6,732.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
